steps.caption: Open Companies in the sidebar and choose Nimbus Ledger Systems, a demo client.
Near the top is the Intelligence panel. The summary says: one live requirement, one deal, two open promises.
Click it to open the account's memory.
First, what is NOT known: industry and current offices. Unknown stays unknown — nothing is guessed.
The summary is built only from the records below. Here AI is off, so it is marked 'rule-based'. Check sources before relying on it.
Important changes: seven differences found in this account's records. Open the list.
Each change shows the old value crossed out, the new value, the date, how sure we are, the source and how many deals it affects.
Recommendations: suggested next steps with the reason and sources. Nothing is done for you.
For example: the requirement area changed by 50%, so refresh the shortlist and comparison.
Overview and current requirements: the live brief and whether the client confirmed it.
Decision-makers and contacts: who decides now, and who has left the company — Rahul Bhide, the old CFO.
Deals: open and earlier deals stay with the company, even when a contact moves on.
Occupancy and rent history: no leases are recorded, so occupancy is shown as unknown.
Relationship history: every recorded conversation, newest first. 'Full timeline' opens them all with filters.
Outstanding commitments: promises we made and when they were due. Red means overdue.
Objections the client raised — here, limited parking — with a link to the conversation.
Recent developments (news and signals) and unresolved questions still to ask the client.
Every line links to its source, so you can always check where a fact came from.
